style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a weathered brushed steel surface. Extreme asymmetric off-centre framing. Two recognisable engineered parts: a network storage drive module and an unlatched inspection gate left visibly open. The parts are arranged in a deliberate tiered stack, constructed from matte textured polymer and frosted copper components. One harsh directional key light throws a long, stretching cast shadow across the steel surface, emphasizing the exposed open gate. Muted modern editorial palette, clean hard edges, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, printed words, watermarks, UI, text
rationale: The story is about a single failure point—an unapplied patch—in a home storage environment. A component assembly of a modular drive bay with an unlatched gate captures the physical metaphor of an open, vulnerable personal server without resorting to literal hacking cliches.
cue: 45 days from notice to public exploit
subject: an unlatched modular drive bay
core_thesis: The real cost of self-hosting is the dangerous 45-day gap between a free patch release and public exploit on an unmaintained home server.
core_conflict: Free setup weekend vs the ongoing operational security debt of unpatched software
